title: Design of experiments as a Wikipedia planning node
dek: Encyclopedia DoE: randomise, block, factorialize. Simplfy already has randomization, blocking, and factorial plates — this is the category glue.
story: Design of experiments on Wikipedia is a planning category: how you assign treatments, block nuisance factors, and structure factorial grids so that the likelihood you intended is the one you can actually fit.

stats-randomization, stats-blocking, and stats-factorial already teach those verbs. This card is the encyclopedia umbrella they sit under, plus a reminder that observational TB genomics is usually not a designed experiment.
NIST's handbook chapters on design are definitional authority. Wikipedia supplies names (CRD, RCBD, Latin square, split-plot).
deep: You cannot ANOVA your way out of confounding that the design never broke (stats-confounding).
Split-plots and repeated measures have two error strata; 'just OLS' is a trap.
Lab plate layouts (inoculum batch, incubator shelf) are blocks whether you named them or not.
Latin squares get a sibling glossary card.
